labels.name: Primary Text
labels.gloss: A direct passage from an ancient, medieval, religious, philosophical, scientific, ritual, or esoteric source, with translation and textual uncertainties noted where relevant.

labels.name: Historical Doctrine
labels.gloss: An interpretation grounded in the documented teachings of a particular person, school, culture, or period.

labels.name: Scientific Evidence
labels.gloss: Information supported by established observation, experimentation, or current scientific scholarship.

labels.name: Phenomenological Report
labels.gloss: A description of lived or reported experience, without claiming that one interpretation has been conclusively established.

labels.name: Architecture of Hidden Forces Doctrine
labels.gloss: Principles belonging specifically to this system — its vocabulary, models, laws, and metaphysical synthesis.

labels.name: Comparative Parallel
labels.gloss: A meaningful resemblance between traditions, with their historical and doctrinal differences preserved.

labels.name: Speculative Extension
labels.gloss: A hypothesis or creative development that remains open to examination, refinement, rejection, or future support.

confidence.name: Established
confidence.gloss: Strongly supported within the relevant field.

confidence.name: Probable
confidence.gloss: Supported by substantial evidence but not certain.

confidence.name: Contested
confidence.gloss: Subject to meaningful scholarly or interpretive disagreement.

confidence.name: Speculative
confidence.gloss: Proposed as a possibility rather than a demonstrated conclusion.

confidence.name: Symbolic
confidence.gloss: A claim made upon the symbolic or correspondential level — disclosing quality, meaning, participation, and formative pattern — not to be converted directly into a physical claim, nor dismissed as unreal because it is not one.

movement.gloss: Where light is what it is before it is given.
The giving — light leaving the source without leaving it poorer.
What it crosses, and what the crossing costs.
The boundary at which difference becomes quality.
Light held in a form, at the form’s measure.
A receiver of the same nature as what it receives.
What light does to what holds it, and what holding does to the light.
The seer, not the light, turned back toward the source.
